_validation_note: BROADENED 45-DAY WINDOW APPLIED (April 6 – May 21, 2026) per fallback protocol after 30-day window (April 21 – May 21) returned zero Gate 3 survivors. Two new candidates evaluated in the April 6–20 gap. CANDIDATE A (Nathan Engel / Alaska Airlines / Tailsight, April 16, 2026): Cleared Gates 1, 2, 5, 6, 7, and conflict screen. Gate 3 (Anchorage tie) marginal: primary source lists Anchorage as one of seven hubs with no Anchorage-specific maintenance language; AI consequence is genuine and fleet-wide but bowl-specific impact is inferential, not named on the fetched page. Gate 4 is a hard fail and determinative drop reason: AviationPros confirmed on fetch as a press release reprint with no reporter byline; StockTitan confirmed as a press release aggregator; every other outlet attempted (ADN, AlaskaJournal, GeekWire, TechCrunch, SimpleFlying, FlightGlobal, AviationWeek, ch-aviation, RunwayGirlNetwork, BusinessTravelNews, SeekingAlpha) returned HTTP 404, 403, or 503. Gate 4 requires at least one independently reported source confirmed on a live fetch; that threshold is not met. CANDIDATE B (NFWF/NOAA Fisheries AI Grant, April 9, 2026): Gate 1 fails — fetched NFWF press release names only federal officials, neither Anchorage-bowl-based; detailed recipient list URL returned 404. 30-day candidates (Wailand, Volland) remain dropped on prior Gate 3 failures. Result: The Anchorage AI decision pool is small and press-release-only coverage of a genuine AI deployment (Engel/Tailsight) is the defining constraint this cycle — the decision may be real but it has not been independently reported and cannot be profiled under the desk's corroboration standard.
